title: Adaptive priority routing with quota smoothing and soft fallbacks
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current tier routing picks targets purely by static priority (enterprise > paid > free) and immediate quota checks. That causes two issues under bursty traffic: (1) paid/enterprise pools get overloaded while free traffic is denied even if paid customers have spare burst capacity, and (2) rapid oscillation between targets when quotas are near limits leads to elevated latency and repeat retries. Goal: implement an adaptive, quota-aware priority router that smooths quota consumption and performs cost-aware soft fallbacks to model variants rather than hard rejects.
proposed_solution: 1) Maintain per-API-key soft quota estimates with an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) of recent token consumption to predict near-term quota pressure. 2) Compute a dynamic priority score per request: base tier score + freshness bonus + quota headroom multiplier + regional affinity penalty. 3) If the top-scored target has predicted quota shortfall within the next 30s, route to a compatible fallback (lower-cost or quantized model variant) rather than immediate failure. 4) Introduce a smoothing window (configurable, default 15s) to avoid thrash when quotas hover. 5) Add a short-term borrowing mechanism: enterprise customers can loan a limited fractional share of their burst capacity to paid tier for critical traffic when governed by policy. 6) Expose knobs in Dedicated/Private consoles to tune smoothing, headroom thresholds, and borrowing rules.
acceptance_criteria: Router computes dynamic priority score and selects candidate target within 5ms median decision time
Requests near tier quotas are routed to fallback model variant rather than hard failure in >= 90% of simulated bursts
No more than 10% latency regression for enterprise SLAs compared to baseline during normal load
Configurable smoothing window and headroom threshold exposed in console and API
End-to-end tests and chaos tests validate behavior under quota depletion and region outage
Telemetry surfaces per-tier headroom, fallback rate, and borrower events in Console dashboards
design_notes_and_tradeoffs: EWMA prediction vs full RL policy: EWMA is simpler and explainable for first rollout; offers deterministic behavior and easy tuning.
Borrowing introduces multi-tenant billing complexity and potential billing disputes; start with opt-in tenant-level flag and tight caps.
Smoothing window reduces oscillation but can increase short-lived over-consumption; choose default 15s and monitor with telemetry.
Fallbacks prefer model variants that preserve quality tier (quantized/gpt-medium) rather than simple downscaling of temperature or truncation.
Regional affinity penalty ensures we do not route high-sensitivity enterprise data to lower-compliance regions; policy must override borrowing/fallbacks for compliance-bound customers.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Simulation harness + algorithm prototype (ENG): implement EWMA headroom, dynamic scoring, fallback selection in simulator
Phase 2: Router integration (ENG): wire into smart-router service with canary flag, add metrics and tracing hooks
Phase 3: Console + API (PM/Console): add controls to tune smoothing/window/headroom, display headroom metrics
Phase 4: Load testing and chaos (SRE/QA): validate under mixed traffic, region failover, and billing events
Phase 5: Gradual rollout and opt-in borrowing beta with select enterprise customers

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Borrowing could be exploited to escape limits. Mitigation: enforce strict caps, audit logs, and billing reconciliation batch jobs.
Risk: Fallbacks may degrade quality and cause customer complaints. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and allow tenant-level opt-out for fallbacks.
Risk: Decision latency increases with scoring complexity. Mitigation: keep scoring arithmetic lightweight and precompute static components; target <5ms decision median.
